newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE says new coffee rules backed by members.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE says new coffee rules backed by members.

text.p: LIFFE said on Tuesday its new coffee grading rules, which have been a cause of worry to some sections of the trade, have been endorsed by its members.
Responding to a Reuters query, an exchange spokesperson said: "As far as we are concerned, we have the support from market participants both users and members."
The new grading terms take effect with the July contract.
LIFFE's May coffee futures have been under sharp selling pressure over the past days ahead of the contract's first tender day on Thursday.
May's discount to July widened to $68 a tonne by late Tuesday trade from $50 on Monday as players liquidated their May positions.
"I think the concerns there are purely on the technical issue on grading the coffee and re-grading the coffee. If you take up May you are not sure you can re-tender it in July," said a trader.
"That's what driven the switch to a big discount, bigger than it should really be ," he said.
Under the rules, current grading specifications would be valued for deliveries until May but all previously graded coffee would have to be re-graded for delivery from July onwards.
When the exchange announced snap changes last December, the premium on the May contract against July shrunk to zero from $15 on the news. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
